meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.

Okay. Your own procedure says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, so I'm glad you said it before I did. What I want to know is what you based the zero on, and whether Owen was ever asked about it.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Go ahead, Hale. I'm reading every page, and I'm writing down the dates.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Owen told me he wrote this over the weekend, so I want to know whether that is the complete history or only the pages you chose to print. And did you put any of this in front of Owen before the zero went in?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
Okay, so the history starts Wednesday night. That tells me where the file begins, not where Owen wrote it. What else do you have besides this one document?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale. That is what an outline is for. Do you have the outline with you, and did Owen ever get to explain the change before the zero went in?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'll search the play myself tonight, and I'm writing that line down. A misquoted line is a weak essay, Hale, not proof of anything about Owen. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Okay. Then a document is all you have, and a document is what the zero was entered on, before Owen was heard. The zero comes off today, Hale. What exactly are you proposing?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Turn it so I can read both. I'm writing down September 24. Tell me what you say the difference is, Hale, and point to where.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Okay, I have 4.4 in my bag, and I'm noting you skipped what the September 24 page shows. If there is a rewrite, it's private, not in front of his class, and "nothing goes on file" comes to me in writing before it happens. When and where, Hale?
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Lunch in your room, not in front of his class. I'm writing that down. Which day, what happens to the zero until then, and when do I get "nothing goes on file" in writing?
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

You don't ask me that, you answer my questions, but fine. The zero comes out of the gradebook today, the day of the rewrite is named in an email, and that email says nothing goes on file and the rewrite mark replaces the original. If I have all three in writing by tomorrow, I'll put this behind him.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. Copy the principal on it. And the email names the day of the rewrite and says the zero is out of the gradebook, not just that you'll look at it.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Yes. Owen hears about the rewrite from you, privately, and nothing about this is said in front of his class. That goes in the email too.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Okay. By eight tonight, and I'll read it carefully.
Thank you for coming in.
Eight o'clock, Hale. I'll be waiting for it.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Tomorrow, Wednesday, at lunch. I'm writing that down, and it goes in the email.
